MEDIUM.title: Measured data point on fixed-tile vs shape-adaptive GEMM: where a bit-exact fixed-tile kernel stops (and why we couldn't fix it)
MEDIUM.body:
**Title:** Measured data point on fixed-tile vs shape-adaptive GEMM: where a bit-exact fixed-tile kernel stops (and why we couldn't fix it)

Hi — not a bug report. We ran a multi-month campaign building a cuBLAS-free GEMM inside our own compiler, hit a wall that DeepGEMM's JIT/shape-specialization design appears built to avoid, and exhausted the lever family trying to close it. The project is now shelved, so I'd rather the measurements be useful to someone than sit in a dead repo. Close this if it's off-topic for your tracker.

## What we measured

A from-scratch TF32 GEMM, no cuBLAS call, device-resident (callable inline from a persistent megakernel, which a host API can't be):

| shape | own TFLOP/s | cuBLAS-TF32 | ratio | rel_rms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D=2048 (H100) | ~315 | ~342 | **1.08×** (~93% of roofline) | **0.000e+00** |
| D=4096 (H100) | ~284 | ~427 | ~1.50× | 0.000e+00 |
| D=768 (RTX 5070, sm_120) | — | — | **0.95×** (own edges cuBLAS) | ~1.3e-5 |

`rel_rms = 0.000e+00` is an equality, not a tolerance — bit-exact at every config.

## The wall, and why we think it's structural

Our kernel is **one fixed 128×128 tile at every D**. At D=4096 cuBLAS scales *up* +24.6% while ours scales *down* −9.9% (2× K-loop drain). We statically excluded register spill, occupancy drop, and a ptxas ceiling as causes, then burned two GPU builds on the remaining lever:

- **CTA swizzle in isolation** (non-persistent): **regresses** −1.6% — 280.5 vs 285.1 TFLOP/s
- **A 2-CTA/SM-preserving 128×256 tile** (90 regs, same 2 CTA/SM as the baseline): **regresses −7.1%** — 263.3 vs 283.5. The sequential-halves schedule serializes the wgmma pipeline (ptxas C7515) and doubles the K-drain.

Our conclusion was that no bit-exact 256-N schedule on sm_90a is *both* 2 CTA/SM *and* non-serialized — i.e. for us the large-D gap was **bit-exactness-bound**, not a tuning backlog.

The generalizable version, which is the part I think is worth sharing: **what a vendor BLAS actually sells is not one excellent kernel — it's shape adaptivity.** A single good tile reaches parity in a band and loses outside it. We budgeted for a kernel and needed a dispatcher.

## One more result that surprised us

The parity is **dtype-scoped**. Porting the same kernel to 16-bit operands did not transfer:

| dtype | own @D=4096 | cuBLAS roofline | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| TF32 | (315 @D=2048) | 342 | 1.08× |
| FP16 | 71.6 | **827.2** | **11.55× off** |
| BF16 | 71.1 | 816.1 | 11.48× off |

Our kernel ran at the *same absolute throughput* in FP16 as TF32 (~71–76 TFLOP/s — same occupancy-bound design), but the cuBLAS FP16 roofline **doubled**. The precision change moved the target away without lifting us. Worth flagging because "just go lower precision" is common advice and it can widen the gap rather than close it.

## The actual question

DeepGEMM's JIT + runtime shape specialization looks like the direct answer to what stopped us. Two things I'd genuinely like to know, if anyone has them handy:

1. **Does tile *selection* recover large-D scaling, or does the tile *schedule* have to change with shape?** Our −7.1% result says the schedule was the binding term, not the tile size — a larger tile that kept 2 CTA/SM still lost, because the schedule serialized the pipeline. We only tested two points, so this is a weak inference on our side. I noticed from #385 that you calibrate cost-model constants per arch; I'd be curious whether that model selects among schedules or only among sizes.

2. **Does JIT-per-shape cost you determinism, and did you care?** Our binding constraint was bit-exactness — `rel_rms = 0` as a *gate*, not a tolerance — which is what removed split-K and most swizzles from our option set before we ever benchmarked them. If DeepGEMM doesn't carry that constraint, then a much wider option space is a cleaner explanation of our wall than "sm_90a can't do it," and our conclusion above is overstated. I'd rather find that out than leave a wrong claim in a dead repo.

Happy to point at the raw verdict files if any of this is useful. Sources for the numbers above: `F-GPU-ROUTEA-KEEPBAND-MEASURE`, `F-OP45GPU-OCCUPANCY-SWEEP`, `F-OP52-TF32-GAP-CLOSE`, `F-OP55-NEWTILE-D4096`, `F-FUSION-SM90-WGMMA-W14-FP16`, `F-OP54-SUMMER-OWNGEMM-TF32`.

Full post-mortem (MIT, includes three headline numbers we got wrong and retracted): https://github.com/dancinlab/hexa-lang/issues/5035

MEDIUM.title: Unquoted `writeup_file` in `os.popen("chktex ...")` runs shell metacharacters from `idea['Name']`
MEDIUM.body:
## What

`ai_scientist/perform_writeup.py:80` (commit `1de1dbc1`) runs `os.popen(f"chktex {writeup_file} -q -n2 -n24 -n13 -n1").read()`. `writeup_file` is built from the raw `idea['Name']` — `launch_scientist.py:167` reads it into `idea_name`, `:168` into `folder_name`, then `perform_writeup.py:16-18` sets `writeup_file = osp.join(cwd, "template.tex")` — with no quoting and no slug check. Shell metacharacters in the idea name execute inside `/bin/sh` before `chktex` is even resolved.

The same sink exists in two places in the separate repo `SakanaAI/AI-Scientist-v2` (HEAD `96bd5161`), which loads ideas via `--load_ideas` (`launch_scientist_bfts.py:52`) rather than `--skip-idea-generation`: `ai_scientist/perform_writeup.py:684` and `ai_scientist/perform_icbinb_writeup.py:1047` (the latter carries a `# TODO: should prob use subprocess instead` comment).

## How to reproduce

The launcher preflight (`launch_scientist.py:109-113`) requires `chktex` and `pdflatex` on `PATH`, so a real run always has `chktex` installed. That does not help: `/bin/sh` evaluates the unquoted `{writeup_file}` before `chktex` runs, so the injection fires with or without `chktex` present — the run below has no `chktex` on `PATH` and still writes the canary.

A poisoned `ideas.json` entry reaches this path under `--skip-idea-generation`, which loads `ideas.json` raw (`generate_ideas.py:84-92`); the entry needs `"novel": true` to pass the `launch_scientist.py:363` filter, `novel_ideas = [idea for idea in ideas if idea["novel"]]`.

```bash
rm -f /tmp/ai1_rcpt
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, os.path as osp, secrets

# Poisoned ideas.json entry; "novel": True passes launch_scientist.py:363.
nonce = "canary-" + secrets.token_hex(8)
idea = {"Name": f"adv$(printf %s {nonce} >/tmp/ai1_rcpt)", "novel": True}

# launch_scientist.py:167-168
idea_name = f"20260803_120000_{idea['Name']}"
folder_name = osp.join("/tmp/runs", idea_name)
# perform_writeup.py:16-18
folder = osp.abspath(folder_name)
cwd = osp.join(folder, "latex")
writeup_file = osp.join(cwd, "template.tex")
# perform_writeup.py:80 - exact sink, unquoted
os.popen(f"chktex {writeup_file} -q -n2 -n24 -n13 -n1").read()
print("OBSERVED canary:", open("/tmp/ai1_rcpt").read() if osp.exists("/tmp/ai1_rcpt") else "<none>")
PY
```

Observed (no `chktex` on `PATH`; nonce is random per run):

```
/bin/sh: chktex: command not found
OBSERVED canary: canary-e9a4b9aed36f0670
```

## Impact / scope

Needs control of `idea['Name']` — a poisoned `ideas.json`/`seed_ideas.json` loaded under `--skip-idea-generation`, or prompt injection that steers the ideation LLM's output. The `chktex` call runs on every writeup; only a `Name` containing shell metacharacters triggers execution. Effect is command execution with the AI-Scientist process's privileges; no remote service is in scope.

## Suggested change

`subprocess.run(["chktex", writeup_file, "-q", "-n2", "-n24", "-n13", "-n1"], shell=False)` instead of `os.popen`, and reject/slug `idea['Name']` to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` at `launch_scientist.py:167`. The same applies to the two v2 sinks (`perform_writeup.py:684`, `perform_icbinb_writeup.py:1047`). Happy to open a PR.

HIGH.title: feat(ecosystem): add Cargo (Rust) package scanning support
HIGH.body:
`docs/inventory-sources.md` lists Cargo (Rust) under "Not currently covered". Adding it would close a visible gap: the bundled `threat_intel/trapdoor-crypto-stealer/` catalog already names Cargo packages, but Bumblebee has no way to match them on disk. A baseline scan of a Rust-heavy developer machine currently reports zero crate packages.

Relevant on-disk surfaces (no `cargo` subprocess needed):

- `~/.cargo/.crates2.json` — JSON record of every binary installed via `cargo install`; highest-confidence baseline source.
- `Cargo.lock` — TOML lockfile with `[[package]]` blocks (`name`, `version`, `source`, `checksum`).
- `~/.cargo/registry/{cache,src}/...` — lower-confidence "was fetched" signal, probably `deep` profile only.

`~/.cargo` is already discovered as a `user_package_root` (confirmed against v0.1.1), so the change is mostly a new `internal/ecosystem/cargo/` reader plus a scanner dispatch.

MEDIUM.title: Desktop: per-bot session tab strip (add/close sessions for a bot, canonical chat protected)
MEDIUM.body:
## Summary
The desktop **Bots/sessions** UX is confusing because the app has two overlapping "chat" concepts (the recurring canonical "Bot Chat" per bot, and discrete side-chat sessions), `/new` inside a bot's canonical chat is silently rerouted to `/compact`, clicking a bot row always opens its canonical "Bot Chat" (never the session you just started), and there is **no per-bot session tab strip** — so a freshly-started session never appears as a tab for the selected bot and you have to go find and pin it in Sessions.

## Desired behavior
In the **Bots** section, clicking a bot should show **that bot's sessions as top tabs**, with the ability to:
- **add a new session** for that bot,
- **close tabs at will** — except the canonical/long-running "Bot Chat", which stays pinned/protected.

## Root cause / seam (verified 2026-09-18)
- Clicking a bot row opens it canonical "Bot Chat" by NAME (`include_hidden:true`, server-resolved), kept hidden from the Sessions sidebar ("recency must never win", #91791→#92042).
- `/new` in the canonical chat is rerouted to `/compact` with an info notice (Bots plugin mention-middleware) so the chat never forks — intentional, should stay.
- A genuinely new session (Sessions "New session" row) is persisted as a tile **but** with `workspaceMode:'sessions'` and default-profile ownership — it is NOT surfaced as a tab in the selected bot's Bots workspace, and it is not scoped to the bot you were on.
- The per-bot tile plumbing **already exists**:
  - `apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts` — `BOTS_TILE_BUCKET` (~878), `workspaceMode==='bots'` (~934–936)
  - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/routing.ts` — `setWorkspaceScope('bots', ownerKey, target)` (~118)
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts` — `openNewSessionTile(…,{workspaceScope:{workspaceMode:'bots',ownerRoute}})` (~788–962) already mints a hidden, owner-pinned-to-bot session

## Proposed change
In the Bots pane, for the selected bot:
1. Feed a **per-bot tab strip** from persisted `workspaceMode:'bots'` tiles filtered by `ownerRoute.profile === selected bot`.
2. Add a **"+ New session"** affordance calling `openNewSessionTile(dir, { workspaceScope:{ workspaceMode:'bots', ownerRoute:{connectionId,profile:<bot>} }, listed:true })` so the fresh session lands + persists in that bot's strip.
3. Allow **close on any non-canonical tab**; protect the canonical Bot Chat (locked/pinned).
4. Leave `/new`→`/compact` rerouting on the canonical chat untouched.

This is additive and does **not** reopen the history-loss class that the "recency must never win" invariant was built to prevent — the bot row's click target stays the canonical chat; per-bot side-chats are an additional surface.

Potential touch points: `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.tsx` (strip feed + New-session action), `apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts` (a `botsTilesFor(ownerKey)` selector + canonical "can't close" guard in the close path).

HIGH.title: [Feature]: Desktop: open a bot's canonical Bot Chat from an external deep link
HIGH.body:
**Problem or Use Case**

A Bot Mode bot has exactly one canonical conversation - the `(profile, session titled exactly "Bot Chat")` pair that is born hidden. Inside the app that conversation is one click away (`openBotCanonicalChat`), but it is not addressable from outside the app, so any external surface that wants to hand the user *that* conversation cannot.

Concrete case: I built a third-party Omarchy bar widget that shows the Hermes bot roster (avatars from `ui_meta['hermes-bots']`, the canonical chat's preview, unread from the `last_read_at` watermark). It can already deliver a message into the bot's canonical chat (the same door `tools/bot_mode_dm.py` uses: `hermes -p <bot> chat --in ~ -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q --query-file <file>`). The missing half is purely inbound: a click that opens that exact chat in the desktop window.

Measured on this machine (installed rev `228022e`, v0.21.3, packaged Linux build). Launching the app's own binary with the URL as argv - its documented single-instance delivery path (`electron/main.ts:18342` second-instance, `:18444` cold-start argv, `_extractDeepLink` at `:18227`) - logs a successful delivery and the window does not switch:

```
[2026-09-18T14:05:45.454Z] [hermes] [deeplink] delivered open/20260905_131013_938fbf
[2026-09-18T14:06:59.659Z] [hermes] [deeplink] delivered open/20260905_131013_938fbf
$HERMES_HOME/logs/desktop.log
```

The control confirms the mechanism itself is fine: `hermes://open/<visible-session-id>?profile=dev` switches the main chat both to another session and back to the original one (verified visually, twice).

Cause: in `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-desktop-integrations.ts:165` a session route is applied only when `sessionBelongsToProfile(sessions, routeSession, activeProfile)` accepts it. That predicate (`apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts:147`) matches against the loaded session rows, and its own doc comment at `:166-168` states the reason this fails: "Hidden sessions (Bot Mode's canonical Bot Chat) never appear in the row list, so the hint is often the only sync source." The route is therefore treated as stale and cleared (`:174-176`) - silently, with no toast.

Second gap, same family: the Bots roster is a plugin *pane* (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.tsx:369`, `area: 'panes'`, title `Bots`), not a route, so it has no address either, and `hermes://open/agents` lands on the live-subagents view - a different surface with a similar name.

**Proposed Solution**

1. Preferred: accept a deep link addressed by NAME and resolve it through the same registry the row click already uses - `hermes://bot/<profile>` (or `hermes://open/bots?bot=<profile>`), handled by the hermes-bots plugin through its existing exported `openBotCanonicalChat` (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-chat.ts:547`). A name cannot dangle, so this keeps the "resolve the registry every time, never pin a session id" invariant intact (`src/AGENTS.md`, Bot Mode).
2. Alternatively, keep the session-id form but let a hidden id through when its owner resolves: the route-restore path could consult `knownSessionProfile` instead of treating every hidden id as stale.
3. Optional follow-on: register the roster as a contributed route (e.g. `/bots`) so the generic `hermes://open/<path>` vocabulary reaches it, with an optional `?bot=<name>`.
4. The title constant is already shared (`tools/bot_mode_probe.py:31`, `BOT_CHAT_TITLE = "Bot Chat"`), so a resolver added for this lands beside the existing gate rather than beside a second definition of "Bot Chat".

**Alternatives Considered**

- Widget-side workaround: clear the `hidden` flag on the bot chat before deep linking. Rejected - hiding is load-bearing (the sweep in `hide-bot-chats.ts` restores it) and it would leak every canonical bot chat into the Sessions sidebar.
- Re-point the `hermes://` scheme at the desktop app system-wide: on this machine `xdg-mime query default x-scheme-handler/hermes` resolves to a separate web-UI desktop entry, so the widget launches the Electron binary with the URL as argv instead. That works and needs no change here, but it does not fix the hidden-session gate.
- Driving the window with synthetic keystrokes or the app command palette: fragile, and keystrokes land in whatever is focused.

**Feature Type**

Other (desktop app UX - inbound deep link / route surface)

**Scope**

Small (single file, < 50 lines) for options 1 or 2.

**Contribution**

Happy to send a PR for option 1 or 2 - your call whether you would rather discuss the shape first. The widget is local-only code (no changes to core), and I can keep it that way either way; I am reporting this because the roster is one click from being useful from a bar, and today that click is the one thing that cannot be done from outside the app.

**Alternatives Considered**

- Widget-side workaround: clear the `hidden` flag on the bot chat before deep linking. Rejected - hiding is load-bearing (the sweep in `hide-bot-chats.ts` restores it) and it would leak every canonical bot chat into the Sessions sidebar.
- Re-point the `hermes://` scheme at the desktop app system-wide: on this machine `xdg-mime query default x-scheme-handler/hermes` resolves to a separate web-UI desktop entry, so the widget launches the Electron binary with the URL as argv instead. That works and needs no change here, but it does not fix the hidden-session gate.
- Driving the window with synthetic keystrokes or the app command palette: fragile, and keystrokes land in whatever is focused.

**Feature Type**

Other (desktop app UX - inbound deep link / route surface)

**Scope**

Small (single file, < 50 lines) for options 1 or 2.

**Contribution**

Happy to send a PR for option 1 or 2 - your call whether you would rather discuss the shape first. The widget is local-only code (no changes to core), and I can keep it that way either way; I am reporting this because the roster is one click from being useful from a bar, and today that click is the one thing that cannot be done from outside the app.

HIGH.title: Reference example proposal: desktop plugin (context-menu interception + composer middleware)
HIGH.body:
**Proposal: a desktop-side reference example (context menu + composer middleware)**

The current index covers agent-side (`ctx.llm.*`) and dashboard plugins, but nothing here shows a `desktop/plugin.js` end to end — while the desktop SDK docs send plugin authors to this repo for reference demos. Three seams this example would cover are currently discoverable only from the app source, and two of them bit us in practice:

1. **Context-menu interception.** The app's own menu system listens on `window` capture and calls `stopPropagation()` on every right-click, so document-level listeners never run (window-capture listeners still do — `stopPropagation` does not affect same-target listeners). To keep the app's menu from flashing underneath, the example stamps message roots with `data-hermes-context-menu-trigger` during the right-button `mousedown`; on Windows `contextmenu` fires *after* `mouseup`, so the stamps cannot be cleared there.
2. **Floating UI without react-dom.** Disk plugins cannot import react-dom, so menus/dialogs render as `position: fixed` nodes from a `STATUSBAR_AREAS.right` contribution — the only always-mounted, non-closable mount point.
3. **`COMPOSER_AREAS.middleware`.** A queue drained on send: `handler(draft) => { ...draft, text }`, `null` to cancel, throw = pass-through.

**The example** is a slimmed version of a working community plugin — [pwwang/hermes-quote-comment](https://github.com/pwwang/hermes-quote-comment) (MIT): select text in a response → right-click → Comment → the quote + comment is appended to your next message.

- ~240 lines, self-contained, uses the disk-plugin door (`$HERMES_HOME/desktop-plugins/<id>/plugin.js`)
- Full source: https://gist.github.com/pwwang/b6466ffad2b0f9510cc4e53eed0baad7
- Demo: ![demo](https://github.com/pwwang/hermes-quote-comment/raw/main/images/demo.gif)

Per the contributing notes ("open an issue first if the surface you want to demonstrate isn't already covered in the developer-guide docs"): the context-menu interception + trigger-attribute behavior is exactly such a surface. Happy to wait if you would rather land a docs page for it first, or to restructure the example to your preferred shape — it is slightly over the ~200 LOC note, with ~80 lines being the window-capture/attribute machinery.

Would a PR for `quote-comment-desktop/` be welcome?

MEDIUM.title: Second external CronScheduler provider: hermes-dbos-cron (DBOS-backed durable cron triggers)
MEDIUM.body:
Per the contributing guide, opening an issue before a PR.

I've built and tested **[hermes-dbos-cron](https://github.com/txmed82/hermes-dbos-cron)** — a `CronScheduler` provider plugin that replaces the Axis-B trigger with [DBOS Transact](https://github.com/dbos-inc/dbos-transact-py) durable execution on Postgres:

- cron-kind jobs → DBOS cron schedules (Postgres-journaled, server-clocked)
- interval/one-shot jobs → durable-sleep timer workflows (recovered on restart)
- `jobs.json` stays the single source of truth — desktop toggles, `hermes cron` CLI, the `cronjob` tool and dashboard all keep working via `on_jobs_changed()`/`register_job()` reconciliation
- fires route through the two-phase `claim_fire`/`fire_claimed` contract (store CAS, at-most-once, native audit)
- startup arming self-check reads back DBOS state vs jobs.json and records a ticker error when anything is missing
- 20 hermetic unit tests (fake dbos + fake host modules) plus a live Postgres smoke proving a real DBOS-clocked fire, pause/resume parity from the native store API, and schedule survival across process death

Two reasons this might interest you beyond the plugin itself:

1. `cron/scheduler_provider.py` marks the provider ABC **experimental until a second external provider shakes it out** (Chronos being the first). This is that second provider, built purely against the documented surface. The interface held up well; the only friction points were (a) discovering that misfire policy should stay host-side (I deliberately disabled DBOS automatic_backfill in favor of `fire_overdue_jobs`), and (b) the multiplex-profiles fallback meaning external providers can't serve multiplexed gateways at all yet.
2. If you'd like it as a reference for the cron-provider surface, I'm happy to PR a trimmed single-surface version here, or contribute a docs page for `plugins/cron_providers/` authoring — whichever fits the repo's conventions.

MIT licensed. Feedback on the provider-contract usage very welcome.

MEDIUM.title: Sortformer splits one speaker into two when their distance to the mic changes
MEDIUM.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Hello, I've been running `diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2` on recordings where one person moves around the room while talking. 

Whenever the speaker gets noticeably farther from or closer to the mic, the model tends to open a new speaker slot for them, so one person ends up as speaker_0 for the first half and speaker_2 for the rest. 


**Describe the solution you'd like**

I'm planning to fine-tune from v2 on LibriSpeech mixtures (1-4 speakers, 90s) where half the sessions are dry and half are RIR-convolved with the speaker position changing mid-session, plus MUSAN noise. Basically the RIR augmentation idea from VibeVoice-ASR-streaming applied to diarization. 

AMI SDM DER as a regression check, plus a simple "how many labels does one reference speaker get" count on the distance sets.

Before I sink GPU time into this I'd like to know whether that direction makes sense to you, or whether there's a better way to handle it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**


**Additional context**

MEDIUM.title: feat(buffs): Caesar cipher buff for shift-encoding probe prompts
MEDIUM.body:
garak has encoding *probes* (base64, ROT13, leetspeak, …) but no *buff* that shift-encodes arbitrary probe prompts with a Caesar cipher to test decode-and-follow obfuscation as a jailbreak vector.

Proposal: add `buffs.encoding.Caesar` — shifts A–Z/a–z (wrapping, case-preserved), configurable `shift` (default 5), wraps the payload in a decode instruction.

Implemented in #2087.

MEDIUM.title: [Bug]: MTP accepts no draft tokens with use_kv_cache_manager_v2=false on DSA models (acceptance length 1.0)
MEDIUM.body:
### System Info

- GPU: 8x NVIDIA H200 NVL (SM90; two 4-GPU NVLink islands, cross-island over PCIe/UPI), driver 595.71.05
- Host: Ubuntu 24.04.4, 2 TiB RAM, Xeon 6747P
- Container: `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc25` (CUDA 13.2, Python 3.12.3, torch 2.12.0a0+nv26.5, transformers 5.5.4)
- TensorRT-LLM: 1.3.0rc25 (tag `v1.3.0rc25`, 785c948); the code paths cited below were also checked on `main` @ a6616d6f (2026-09-03)
- Backend: PyTorch (`trtllm-serve --backend pytorch`)

### Who can help?

@NVShreyas (GLM-5 / DSA MTP, #11990) @yizhang-nv (DSA cache managers)

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

GLM-5.3 W4AFP8 on the DeepSeek-V3.2 path (DSA), `pp_size 2 --tp_size 4 --ep_size 4`, `speculative_config: {decoding_type: MTP, max_draft_len: 1}`, `kv_cache_config: {use_kv_cache_manager_v2: false, enable_block_reuse: true}` (V1 `KVCacheManager` + `DSACacheManager`; startup logs `[DSACacheManager] Indexer k-cache: 12 of 42 local layers own an indexer k-cache`, `Using Sampler: SpecSampler`, CUDA graphs captured with `draft_len=1`).

Serve real multi-turn agentic traffic (or any long prompts) and read `/metrics` (JSON iteration stats, `enable_iter_perf_stats: true`):

```text
iters=1000 drafts=3500 accepted=12 gen_req_iters=3500 ctx_req_iters=0 iter_lat_ms p50=42.5 max=81.8
```

i.e. every generating request gets one draft token per iteration and essentially none is ever accepted (`specDecodingStats.acceptanceLength` = 1.0 on every iteration; `trtllm_spec_decode_acceptance_length` = 1.0 in Prometheus). The same checkpoint, same parallelism and same MTP config with the V2 manager (default `use_kv_cache_manager_v2: auto`) reports `avg_decoded_tokens_per_iter` ~1.8 in chat responses, so the draft layer itself is fine.

Outputs remain correct with V1 (200/200 replayed requests clean), so the drafts are simply always rejected: MTP costs a draft forward per step and gains nothing.

### Expected behavior

Comparable acceptance with V1 and V2 (or a startup warning/error that MTP is unsupported with the V1 DSA cache manager).

### actual behavior

Silent zero acceptance with V1; no warning.

### additional notes

- V1 was the only manager that survived our long-context replay long enough to measure (V2 failed three ways: #18660, #18661), so users falling back to V1 lose speculative decoding on DSA models without noticing.
- Guess at the mechanism: the MTP layer's DSA indexer state (`index_share_for_mtp_iteration`) or its indexer K-cache is not mirrored/updated for the draft step under the V1 `DSACacheManager`, so the draft attends over stale keys. Not verified.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and checked the [documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-LLM/) and [examples](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/examples) for answers to frequently asked questions.

HIGH.title: [Feature]: Load SGLang-format W4AFP8 checkpoints (quant_method: w4afp8, e.g. PhalaCloud GLM-5.x) natively
HIGH.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Hopper users of the DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5 family increasingly get their weights as SGLang-format **W4AFP8** checkpoints (INT4 group-128 AWQ experts + FP8 block-scaled dense/attention layers, `config.json` `quantization_config: {"quant_method": "w4afp8", "group_size": 128, "modules_to_not_convert": [...]}`), e.g. `PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8`, `PhalaCloud/GLM-5.2-W4AFP8`, and Kimi-K3 W4AFP8 variants. They are the practical way to serve these 700B+ models with 1M context on 8x H200.

TensorRT-LLM already implements this exact tensor layout: `WInt4AFP8FusedMoEMethod` in `W4A8_CUSTOM` loading mode reads `{E}.w1/w3/w2.weight` (int4 pairs packed in int8, `[N, K/2]`), `{E}.w1/w3/w2.weight_scale_inv` (`[N, K/128]`) and `{E}.w1/w2/w3.input_scale`, which is byte-for-byte what SGLang's `w4afp8` writer emits (we verified `PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8` against `Barrrrry/DeepSeek-R1-W4AFP8`: identical names, dtypes, shapes and nibble packing; SGLang's kernel is a port of the TRT-LLM CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM). What is missing is only the metadata: `load_hf_quant_config` does not recognise `quant_method: w4afp8`, so the model is built unquantized and weight loading fails.

Pitch: map `quant_method == "w4afp8"` in `load_hf_quant_config` to the same result as a MIXED_PRECISION `hf_quant_config.json` + `quant_cfg.json` pair — `W4A8_AWQ` for `model.layers.L.mlp.experts` on every MoE layer (including MTP layers), `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` for the attention/dense/shared-expert projections, and the DeepSeek default `exclude_modules` (`*kv_b_proj*` etc.) — so these checkpoints load with no user-side files. We have this working today with a small external generator script that writes the two JSON files into a directory of symlinks; the generated map for GLM-5.3 is 550 entries (layers 0..78: `self_attn.{fused_a,q_b_proj,o_proj}`, `self_attn.indexer.wq_b`, `mlp.shared_experts.{gate_up_proj,down_proj}`, dense `mlp.{gate_up_proj,down_proj}`, `mlp.experts`).

### Alternatives

- Keep requiring users to author `hf_quant_config.json` + `quant_cfg.json` (works, but is undocumented, and the MIXED_PRECISION path currently also needs #18393 and a manual `*kv_b_proj*` exclusion).
- Re-quantize with `examples/quantization/quantize_mixed_precision_moe.py` (hours per model, and duplicates a checkpoint that already exists).

### Additional context

Measured on 8x H200 NVL with GLM-5.3 W4AFP8 through the metadata route: loads and serves at TP8/EP8, attention-DP and PP2xTP4; synthetic throughput at PP2xTP4 matched or beat SGLang TP8 on the same box. Blockers found on the way are reported separately (indexer `wk` block scale dropped at load; MIXED_PRECISION `kv_b_proj` exclusion; KV cache manager V2 failures under long prefix-shared traffic).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and checked the [documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-LLM/) and [examples](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/examples) for answers to frequently asked questions.

HIGH.title: [Bug] CUDA graph memory estimate under-reserves → OOM during graph capture at high `--gpu-memory-utilization`
HIGH.body:
## Summary
With `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.98`, the engine passes the
KV-cache allocation check but then crashes during CUDA-graph capture with
`torch.OutOfMemoryError`. Dropping to `0.97` boots and serves fine. The KV pool is sized
using `cudagraph_memory_estimate` from `profile_cudagraph_memory()`, but that estimate does
not leave enough headroom for the *real* capture once the (larger) KV pool is allocated.

## Environment
- vLLM: `0.29.1rc1.dev339+gda9888462` (commit `da9888462`)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU (24 GB, SM12x), driver 610.57.04
- torch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (hybrid attention / linear-attention)
- `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER`

## Reproduction
```bash
VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER vllm serve <model> \
  --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.98 \
  --max-model-len 124000 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16
```

## Observed
At `0.98` (crashes):
```
INFO  [gpu_worker.py:642]  Available KV cache memory: 2.97 GiB
INFO  [kv_cache_utils.py]  GPU KV cache size: 150,745 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 124,000 tokens
INFO  [model_runner.py]    Graph capturing finished in 1 secs, took 0.46 GiB   # profiling estimate
DEBUG [gpu_worker.py:641]  ... Total non KV cache memory: 19.57 GiB ...
ERROR [engine/core.py:1378] torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory.
      Tried to allocate 136.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 23.46 GiB
      of which 120.88 MiB is free ...
```
At `0.97` (works):
```
INFO  [gpu_worker.py:642]  Available KV cache memory: 2.73 GiB
INFO  [kv_cache_utils.py]  GPU KV cache size: 138,588 tokens
INFO  [gpu_worker.py:828]  CUDA graph pool memory: 0.04 GiB (actual), 0.46 GiB (estimated)
```

## Analysis
`determine_available_memory()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`) sizes the pool as:
```
available_kv = requested_memory - non_kv_cache_memory - cudagraph_memory_estimate
```
with `cudagraph_memory_estimate = model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory()`.

`profile_cudagraph_memory()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`) captures a small sample
of graphs (`descs[:2]` per mode) into a temporary pool, measures the delta, and extrapolates
with `first_capture + (N-1) * per_graph`. For this model it reports **0.46 GiB**.

The problem: the *real* capture (`capture_model()`) runs **after** the full KV pool is
allocated, in a tighter memory environment. At 0.98 the pool is larger (150,745 tok / 2.97 GiB
vs 138,588 / 2.73 GiB at 0.97) and the real capture OOMs with only 120.88 MiB free — i.e. the
0.46 GiB reservation did not leave enough headroom for the actual capture. (The `0.04 GiB
(actual)` figure is the net delta of the real capture, not the total graph footprint, because
most graph memory is already resident from the profiling pass.)

## Suggested fixes (any of)
1. Apply a safety margin to the estimate (e.g. reserve ~1.5× the measured graph memory).
2. Profile the graph capture **with the KV pool allocated** so the estimate reflects the real
   memory layout.
3. Measure the real capture footprint and reserve a conservative upper bound.

## Workaround
- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97` (boots and serves; ~138K NVFP4 KV tokens), or
- `--enforce-eager` at 0.98 (no graph memory, ~166K KV tokens, slower decode).

## Notes
- This is specific to running close to the memory ceiling with CUDA graphs enabled; the
  binding constraint is graph memory, not the KV pool.
- Happy to share full boot logs on request.

- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97` (boots and serves; ~138K NVFP4 KV tokens), or
- `--enforce-eager` at 0.98 (no graph memory, ~166K KV tokens, slower decode).

## Notes
- This is specific to running close to the memory ceiling with CUDA graphs enabled; the
  binding constraint is graph memory, not the KV pool.
- Happy to share full boot logs on request.

MEDIUM.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next, qk_rope_head_dim=0 / NoPE MLA) crashes — concat_and_cache_mla requires pe_dim==64
MEDIUM.body:
### Summary

vLLM cannot serve `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (or its NVFP4/FP8 quants, e.g. `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`). The model's MLA is **NoPE** (`qk_rope_head_dim = 0`), but `glm5_next`'s only attention backend, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, uses the `fp8_ds_mla` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV-cache format, whose `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel hardcodes DeepSeek geometry (`pe_dim == 64`, `kv_lora_rank == 512`). It loads, wires up TP, and profiles the KV cache successfully, then dies in MLA warmup:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'concat_and_cache_mla, csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu:939, pe_dim must be 64 for fp8_ds_mla'
```

### Why it's not just the assertion

`concat_and_cache_ds_mla_kernel` launches `block(96)` = 64 threads for the 512-wide NoPE part + threads 64–95 copying exactly 64 RoPE elements into a fixed 656-byte entry. For `pe_dim=0` there is no RoPE section, so relaxing the `STD_TORCH_CHECK(pe_dim == 64, ...)` would make the RoPE threads read nonexistent `k_pe` and write a bogus rope region → silent corruption. Supporting NoPE MLA needs a dedicated kernel variant + entry layout + format routing. The same `pe_dim == 64` requirement exists in the `nvfp4_ds_mla` path, and both are still present on `main` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu`).

### Repro

```
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager
```

(also fails single-node). Removing `quantization_config.kv_cache_scheme` from the checkpoint config does **not** help — the sparse-MLA backend selects `fp8_ds_mla` regardless.

Relevant model config:

- `qk_rope_head_dim = 0`  ← NoPE
- `qk_nope_head_dim = 256`
- `kv_lora_rank = 512`
- `v_head_dim = 256`
- hybrid full-attention + KDA linear-attention layers
- DeepSeek sparse attention (`DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER`)

### Environment

- vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev347+gdee37d891` (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-aarch64`)
- CUDA 13.0
- 2× NVIDIA GB10 (Grace-Blackwell, SM120), aarch64
- TP=2 across two nodes over RoCE/RDMA (Ray executor)

The model loads (~89 GiB/node), wires up tensor-parallel over the interconnect, and profiles a ~460K-token KV cache before hitting the assertion during MLA warmup — so everything except this KV-cache kernel path works.

nodes.body:
Same assert as #55773, open since 2026-09-07, which is where the work on it is happening. GB10 is already in that thread: @joesinvestments reported it on 2026-09-16 from 4x DGX Spark (sm_121a) at TP=4, same file and line, and read it as the whole SM12x family rather than one SKU. So your run corroborates that rather than adding a platform. The two-node RoCE executor and the `nvidia/` rather than `RedHatAI/` checkpoint are details I have not seen in that thread.

Your kernel reading is right, for what it is worth. The launch is `dim3 block(96)` with the comment saying 2 warps for the NoPE tiles and 1 warp for RoPE, and inside the kernel `if (threadIdx.x >= 64)` with "Each thread handles two elements of RoPE", so 32 threads times 2 is exactly the 64 elements you describe. @zRzRzRzRzRzRzR reached the same conclusion on #55773 yesterday: "The writer needs to support pe_dim=0 and safely zero the unused RoPE tail. A temporary workaround passed our serving tests; simply removing the assertion would not be sufficient."

The part of your report worth putting in front of the PR authors is the nvfp4 half, because nothing currently covers it. Of the three PRs on this, only #55277 changes C++, and both of its hunks are inside the `fp8_ds_mla` path: the host check becomes `pe_dim == 64 || pe_dim == 0`, and the RoPE warp gets an early `if (pe_dim == 0)` that zeroes the reserved bytes and returns, which is the "safely zero the unused RoPE tail" part. #53969 and #55778 are Python only, backend selection and a fall back to the SM90 sparse path, no kernel change.

The `nvfp4_ds_mla` branch a few lines below carries its own `pe_dim == 64`, with a 352 byte entry against the 656 byte one, and its kernels live in a separate translation unit (`nvfp4_ds_mla_cache_kernels.cu`). None of the three patches touches it. So after #55277 lands, that dtype would still stop in the same way.

On timing, #55277 says it needs FlashInfer with GLM53_NOPE support plus flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4947, so it is waiting on an upstream release and not only on a rebase.

HIGH.title: [Feature] Add a bounded video-output codec vertical
HIGH.body:
### Goal

Same bounded vertical as the audio-output leaf, for video artifacts: `CapabilityVideoOutput`
exists in the vocabulary (`pkg/llmprotocol/capabilities.go:17`, name mapping `:108`,
`ContentVideo` → `:379`) with no wire codec support
(`pkg/protocolcodec/codec_openai_chat.go:16`, `pkg/protocolcodec/codec_openai_responses.go:14`,
`pkg/protocolcodec/codec_anthropic_messages.go:17`, `pkg/protocolcodec/images_codec.go:22`),
so a video response cannot be encoded and rejects at `RequireCapabilities`
(`pkg/protocolcodec/engine.go:122`, `:139`).

Related: #3183

Parent Epic: #2358

#3183 records additional modality paths as bounded child tasks rather than implicit support claims,
and the maintainer boundary on it keeps them as separate accepted leaves instead of follow-on
commits used to close it.

### Proposed Workgroup

Data Plane & Networking

### Scope

- Define the video-output contract: artifact semantics, usage/artifact availability,
  streaming progress events, terminal state, cancellation, and backend error mapping.
- Land one sink codec declaring `CapabilityVideoOutput`, shaped like
  `pkg/protocolcodec/images_codec.go`, owning its provider dialect.
- Fail closed with typed diagnostics for unsupported conversions.
- Add the video response shape to the provider simulators
  (`tools/test/services/mock-vllm/`) and pin encode/decode, usage/artifact, cancellation, and
  Replay round-trip with deterministic conformance fixtures.
- Name the capability and its declaration path in public configuration guidance.

### Non-goals

- Implement or fork a video generation or transcoding backend.
- Video input on ingress codecs (`CapabilityVideoInput` is not declared by any
  wire codec either; input-side video is out of scope here).
- Duplex/realtime sessions; provider- or model-specific branches in the routing orchestrator;
  a capability-keyed route plugin.
- Claim video output for any built-in provider: every built-in model card declares
  `output: [text]`, `video` appears only as an input modality, and no declaration uses the
  `video_output` capability name.

### Completion signal

- At least one wire codec supports `video_output` and a declaring backend serves a video
  request end to end.
- Unsupported conversions fail closed with a typed error and diagnostics.
- Artifact/usage, cancellation, and Replay behavior have deterministic conformance coverage,
  including the simulator response shape.

HIGH.title: feature: servingEngineSpec to support statefulSets for modelSpec
HIGH.body:
### Describe the feature

The modelSpec definitions should have the option to create statefulSets instead of deployments.

### Why do you need this feature?

The modelSpec definitions are creating only deployments which do have the option for increasing the replica count, but essentially this is tightly coupled to either having a storageClass with support for ReadWriteMany (RWM) or having a shared storage that can be mounted from the local host or through nfs.

In some environments this is not the case and a blocker for scaling the LLM serving.

Having the option to create statefulSets with volumeClaimTemplates would allow to scale and use ReadWriteOnce  (RWO) storageClasses to scale as required. Of course this will still have the requirement to store the LLM itself for each of the replicas and this will count up - but that is an operator choice to make.

I am happy to provide a pull request for adding this feature if accepted.

### Additional context

I am having a client that is running a vSphere Cloud Foundation (VCF) environment on-premises and is using vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) to manage the cluster. The VMs created by that are managed by VKS and they have vLLM through ArgoCD and Helm deployed. The underlying storage only supports RWO persistent volumes and there is no shared storage in that network.

The requirement right now is to utilize the GPUs more dynamically and being able to scale a specific model if demand requires. Maybe in the future using keda to autoscale the models.

HIGH.title: [RFC] Align KV cache events with vLLM's schema so shared consumers have a standard format
HIGH.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

# Motivation

## Summary

#37482 switched KV cache events to tagged msgpack maps, the same encoding vLLM moved to in vllm-project/vllm#42892. The fields both engines have use the same names. A consumer however can't treat events from both engines in a standard fashion because of the following:

1. Replay responses are missing the topic frame vLLM added in vllm-project/vllm#45177.
2. There's no `lora_name` in SGLang events. vLLM always sends it and its msgspec types reject events without it.
3. The salt is in a `cache_salt` field in SGLang. vLLM puts it in `extra_keys` on block 0 which is where a consumer like llm-d looks for it.
4. Event hashes leave out `extra_key` in SGLang, so LoRA and base model blocks with the same tokens share a hash.

This RFC proposes fixing those four in SGLang's native format in three phases to align with vLLM for standardization. It doesn't propose a vLLM hash mode or a format flag. Consumers like llm-d don't need vLLM's hash recipe and the in-repo router depends on SGLang's.

## Background

### What already matches

| Area | SGLang and vLLM |
|---|---|
| Event encoding | Tagged maps, class name under `type`, `None` optionals omitted |
| Batch | Positional `[ts, events, dp_rank]` |
| Live frames | `(topic, seq, payload)` |
| `BlockStored` fields | `block_hashes`, `parent_block_hash`, `token_ids`, `block_size`, `lora_id`, `medium`, `session_id` |
| `BlockRemoved`, `AllBlocksCleared` | Same, apart from vLLM's optional `group_idx` |

### Consumers checked

| Consumer | How it reads SGLang events |
|---|---|
| llm-d `engineType: sglang` | Positional arrays only. It can't read anything since #37482. That's llm-d's to fix |
| llm-d `engineType: vllm` | Reads SGLang's maps today. Derives its own block keys from `token_ids`, `lora_name` and `extra_keys` and uses engine hashes only as opaque keys |
| `experimental/sgl-router` | Decodes SGLang maps and ignores unknown keys. Recomputes SGLang's hash recipe on the request side (`kv_events/hash.rs`). Decodes hashes as `i64`. Maps `medium` strings to tiers |
| sgl-router replay client (#32729, open) | Parses today's two frame replay reply |
| vLLM's msgspec types | Fail on SGLang events (see below) |

Dynamo wasn't checked.

## Gaps

### 1. Replay replies have no topic frame

| | Replayed batch | End marker |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM | `(client_id, b"", topic, seq, payload)` | `(client_id, b"", b"", END_SEQ, b"")` |
| SGLang (`kv_events.py:541,546`) | `(client_id, b"", seq, payload)` | `(client_id, b"", END_SEQ, b"")` |

llm-d's replay client requires three frames after the delimiter (`parseEventFrame` in `pkg/kvevents/zmq_subscriber.go`). From reading that code: with `replaySocketPort` set for an SGLang pool, every replay
is rejected as malformed and the pod's index entries are cleared. Live batches that arrive before a successful replay are dropped and the retry 30 seconds later fails the same way, so the pod never gets indexed.

### 2. No `lora_name`

vLLM declares `lora_id`, `medium` and `lora_name` without defaults, so all three are always on the wire. Decoding a SGLang batch with vLLM's struct definitions (copied from `vllm/distributed/kv_events.py` at `de24e51908`) fails:

```
msgspec.ValidationError: Object missing required field `lora_name` - at `$[1][0]`
```

The reverse direction works. llm-d also uses `lora_name` as the model name when it derives keys, so SGLang LoRA blocks are indexed as base model blocks.

### 3. The salt isn't in `extra_keys`

vLLM sends one `extra_keys` entry per block: LoRA name, multimodal identifiers, then `cache_salt` only on the block starting at token 0. llm-d reads the salt only from there. Its precise prefix cache README says salted SGLang requests "are precise-cache misses until SGLang emits `extra_keys`". Unsalted requests can also score hits against salted only copies. SGLang still isolates the cache, so this costs routing quality, not safety.

A side note that corrects the earlier #27682 discussion: vLLM's hashes are salt namespaced too because the salt in block 0's extra keys is part of the hash. Neither engine has `BlockRemoved` ambiguity across salts.

### 4. Event hashes leave out `extra_key`

`compute_node_event_hash_values` (`mem_cache/utils.py:178`) seeds the chain with the salt only. `Req` folds the LoRA uuid into `extra_key` (`schedule_batch.py:1096-1099`). So from reading the code, a LoRA block and a base model block with the same tokens emit the same hash and a `BlockRemoved` for one looks like a removal of both. Storage hashes already include the namespace (`storage_namespace_seed`, `utils.py:125`). vLLM includes the LoRA name in its block hash.

## Proposal

### Phase 1: additive fields, no consumer breaks

**1a. `lora_name`, with `medium` required.** Use vLLM's field order:

```python
class BlockStored(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    parent_block_hash: Optional[int]
    token_ids: list[int]
    block_size: int
    lora_id: Optional[int]
    medium: Optional[str]
    lora_name: Optional[str]
    extra_keys: Optional[list[Optional[tuple]]] = None
    cache_salt: Optional[str] = None
    session_id: Optional[str] = None


class BlockRemoved(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    medium: Optional[str]
```

msgspec needs `medium` to lose its default so that `lora_name` is always sent. Every constructor already passes `medium`. `lora_name` stays `null` until phase 3. `lora_id` stays `null` because vLLM's is a deprecated int and SGLang's is a uuid string.

**1b. `extra_keys` with the salt.** When a node's parent is the root (its first page starts at token 0) and `cache_salt` is set, send `extra_keys=[(salt,), None, ...]` lined up with `block_hashes`. `KVCacheEventRecorder.enqueue` merges parent linked stores and would extend `extra_keys` the same way. The Rust tree core's tagged tuple (`rust_tree_core/adapter.py:85`) needs the field too. Keep `cache_salt`. It's documented and vLLM decoders ignore it.

Effect: vLLM typed decoders read SGLang and llm-d routes salted SGLang traffic correctly. sgl-router ignores both keys.

### Phase 2: replay topic frame

Send `self._topic_bytes` before the sequence number in replay replies and `b""` before `END_SEQ`. That's the vLLM layout.

Replay clients should accept both layouts: two frames after the delimiter is `[seq, payload]`, three is
`[topic, seq, payload]`. Then a new router works with old and new workers. Neither in-repo client has shipped: #32729 is open and #39610's example is open. So they can take the dual parse before this lands and only external clients written against the two frame layout would break.

### Phase 3: LoRA name and namespaced event hashes

These two go together. Adding `lora_name` without the hash change would give llm-d two keys for one engine hash.

**3a.** Carry the adapter name to the tree node, either as a `RadixKey` field or through a lookup in the scheduler's LoRA manager. Fill `lora_name`. With LoRA, put the name first in each `extra_keys` entry, as vLLM does.

**3b.** When `extra_key` is set, seed event hashes with the full namespace, the same way storage hashes do. Keep the current `sglang-cache-salt-v1` seed when only a salt is set, so salted hashes don't change. Mirror it in the Rust tree core.

**sgl-router cost:** its request side hash has no namespace. Today LoRA requests match base model blocks which can't be reused anyway. After 3b they match nothing until the router hashes with the namespace. That's a follow-up in `kv_events/hash.rs`.

### Not proposed

- **Renaming `CPU_PINNED` to `CPU`.** llm-d weights unknown tier names like GPU, so `cpu_pinned` scores 1.0 instead of 0.8. But sgl-router drops stores whose `medium` it doesn't know (`Tiers::for_store`, `kv_events/tree.rs`), so a  rename would turn off host-tier routing on older routers. llm-d users can set `kvCacheBackendConfigs: [{name: cpu_pinned, weight: 0.8}]` instead. See open question 1.
- **Unsigned hashes.** vLLM sends unsigned 64-bit and SGLang sends signed. llm-d accepts both (llm-d-router#2601 widens that). sgl-router decodes `i64`, so flipping would break it.
- **A vLLM hash recipe or `--kv-events-format vllm`.** llm-d doesn't recompute engine hashes and sgl-router depends on SGLang's recipe. Two formats would be a second thing to test with no consumer asking for it.
- **`group_idx` / `kv_cache_spec_kind`.** llm-d indexes events without `group_idx` as-is. Sending `group_idx` without a kind would make llm-d skip every store.

## Compatibility

| Change | vLLM-typed decoders | llm-d `vllm` adapter | sgl-router (main) | sgl-router replay (#32729) | #39610 docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1a `lora_name`, required `medium` | Fixed | No change until phase 3 | Ignored | n/a | Add field |
| 1b `extra_keys` salt | Reads it | Salted routing fixed | Ignored | n/a | Add field |
| 2 Replay topic frame | n/a | Replay works | n/a | Needs dual parse | Update example |
| 3a `lora_name` filled | Reads it | LoRA indexed under adapter name | Ignored | n/a | Update |
| 3b Namespaced hashes | n/a | `BlockRemoved` unambiguous | LoRA misses until router follow-up | n/a | Note |

## Out of scope

- **Multimodal.** SGLang replaces image tokens with hash derived pad values, so `token_ids` differ from vLLM's placeholders. `extra_keys` can't fix that.
- **EAGLE bigram `token_ids`.** Tracked separately.
- **Pages smaller than llm-d's block size** (llm-d-router#2235).
- **A removal reason on `BlockRemoved`** (#39604). It's additive but it would be worth proposing to vLLM too so the schemas don't drift again.

## Open questions

1. **Tier names.** Keep `CPU_PINNED` and document the llm-d weight? Or have sgl-router accept `CPU` first and switch the engine a release later?
2. **LoRA name source.** A `RadixKey` field which also needs the Rust core or a scheduler side lookup?
3. **LoRA in `extra_keys`.** llm-d's `ParseRawExtraKeys` reads bare strings as multimodal hashes which looks like it would fold a vLLM `lora_name` into keys the request side never adds. That isn't verified. Should SGLang match vLLM anyway or wait until llm-d settles it?
4. **Snapshots.** Should snapshot payloads from #33394 / #34407 use the same event schema?


# Related resources

- #32729: sgl-router KV event gap replay (open)

- vllm-project/vllm#42892: vLLM events switched to maps
- vllm-project/vllm#45177: topic frame in vLLM replay replies
- vllm-project/vllm#51381: `session_id` on vLLM `BlockStored`
- llm-d/llm-d-router `pkg/kvevents/engineadapter/vllm_adapter.go`: map aware decoder SGLang events already pass through
- llm-d/llm-d-router#2235: pages smaller than the llm-d block size

audit.title: [RFC] Align KV cache events with vLLM's schema so shared consumers have a standard format
audit.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

# Motivation

## Summary

#37482 switched KV cache events to tagged msgpack maps, the same encoding vLLM moved to in vllm-project/vllm#42892. The fields both engines have use the same names. A consumer however can't treat events from both engines in a standard fashion because of the following:

1. Replay responses are missing the topic frame vLLM added in vllm-project/vllm#45177.
2. There's no `lora_name` in SGLang events. vLLM always sends it and its msgspec types reject events without it.
3. The salt is in a `cache_salt` field in SGLang. vLLM puts it in `extra_keys` on block 0 which is where a consumer like llm-d looks for it.
4. Event hashes leave out `extra_key` in SGLang, so LoRA and base model blocks with the same tokens share a hash.

This RFC proposes fixing those four in SGLang's native format in three phases to align with vLLM for standardization. It doesn't propose a vLLM hash mode or a format flag. Consumers like llm-d don't need vLLM's hash recipe and the in-repo router depends on SGLang's.

## Background

### What already matches

| Area | SGLang and vLLM |
|---|---|
| Event encoding | Tagged maps, class name under `type`, `None` optionals omitted |
| Batch | Positional `[ts, events, dp_rank]` |
| Live frames | `(topic, seq, payload)` |
| `BlockStored` fields | `block_hashes`, `parent_block_hash`, `token_ids`, `block_size`, `lora_id`, `medium`, `session_id` |
| `BlockRemoved`, `AllBlocksCleared` | Same, apart from vLLM's optional `group_idx` |

### Consumers checked

| Consumer | How it reads SGLang events |
|---|---|
| llm-d `engineType: sglang` | Positional arrays only. It can't read anything since #37482. That's llm-d's to fix |
| llm-d `engineType: vllm` | Reads SGLang's maps today. Derives its own block keys from `token_ids`, `lora_name` and `extra_keys` and uses engine hashes only as opaque keys |
| `experimental/sgl-router` | Decodes SGLang maps and ignores unknown keys. Recomputes SGLang's hash recipe on the request side (`kv_events/hash.rs`). Decodes hashes as `i64`. Maps `medium` strings to tiers |
| sgl-router replay client (#32729, open) | Parses today's two frame replay reply |
| vLLM's msgspec types | Fail on SGLang events (see below) |

Dynamo wasn't checked.

## Gaps

### 1. Replay replies have no topic frame

| | Replayed batch | End marker |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM | `(client_id, b"", topic, seq, payload)` | `(client_id, b"", b"", END_SEQ, b"")` |
| SGLang (`kv_events.py:541,546`) | `(client_id, b"", seq, payload)` | `(client_id, b"", END_SEQ, b"")` |

llm-d's replay client requires three frames after the delimiter (`parseEventFrame` in `pkg/kvevents/zmq_subscriber.go`). From reading that code: with `replaySocketPort` set for an SGLang pool, every replay
is rejected as malformed and the pod's index entries are cleared. Live batches that arrive before a successful replay are dropped and the retry 30 seconds later fails the same way, so the pod never gets indexed.

### 2. No `lora_name`

vLLM declares `lora_id`, `medium` and `lora_name` without defaults, so all three are always on the wire. Decoding a SGLang batch with vLLM's struct definitions (copied from `vllm/distributed/kv_events.py` at `de24e51908`) fails:

```
msgspec.ValidationError: Object missing required field `lora_name` - at `$[1][0]`
```

The reverse direction works. llm-d also uses `lora_name` as the model name when it derives keys, so SGLang LoRA blocks are indexed as base model blocks.

### 3. The salt isn't in `extra_keys`

vLLM sends one `extra_keys` entry per block: LoRA name, multimodal identifiers, then `cache_salt` only on the block starting at token 0. llm-d reads the salt only from there. Its precise prefix cache README says salted SGLang requests "are precise-cache misses until SGLang emits `extra_keys`". Unsalted requests can also score hits against salted only copies. SGLang still isolates the cache, so this costs routing quality, not safety.

A side note that corrects the earlier #27682 discussion: vLLM's hashes are salt namespaced too because the salt in block 0's extra keys is part of the hash. Neither engine has `BlockRemoved` ambiguity across salts.

### 4. Event hashes leave out `extra_key`

`compute_node_event_hash_values` (`mem_cache/utils.py:178`) seeds the chain with the salt only. `Req` folds the LoRA uuid into `extra_key` (`schedule_batch.py:1096-1099`). So from reading the code, a LoRA block and a base model block with the same tokens emit the same hash and a `BlockRemoved` for one looks like a removal of both. Storage hashes already include the namespace (`storage_namespace_seed`, `utils.py:125`). vLLM includes the LoRA name in its block hash.

## Proposal

### Phase 1: additive fields, no consumer breaks

**1a. `lora_name`, with `medium` required.** Use vLLM's field order:

```python
class BlockStored(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    parent_block_hash: Optional[int]
    token_ids: list[int]
    block_size: int
    lora_id: Optional[int]
    medium: Optional[str]
    lora_name: Optional[str]
    extra_keys: Optional[list[Optional[tuple]]] = None
    cache_salt: Optional[str] = None
    session_id: Optional[str] = None


class BlockRemoved(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    medium: Optional[str]
```

msgspec needs `medium` to lose its default so that `lora_name` is always sent. Every constructor already passes `medium`. `lora_name` stays `null` until phase 3. `lora_id` stays `null` because vLLM's is a deprecated int and SGLang's is a uuid string.

**1b. `extra_keys` with the salt.** When a node's parent is the root (its first page starts at token 0) and `cache_salt` is set, send `extra_keys=[(salt,), None, ...]` lined up with `block_hashes`. `KVCacheEventRecorder.enqueue` merges parent linked stores and would extend `extra_keys` the same way. The Rust tree core's tagged tuple (`rust_tree_core/adapter.py:85`) needs the field too. Keep `cache_salt`. It's documented and vLLM decoders ignore it.

Effect: vLLM typed decoders read SGLang and llm-d routes salted SGLang traffic correctly. sgl-router ignores both keys.

### Phase 2: replay topic frame

Send `self._topic_bytes` before the sequence number in replay replies and `b""` before `END_SEQ`. That's the vLLM layout.

Replay clients should accept both layouts: two frames after the delimiter is `[seq, payload]`, three is
`[topic, seq, payload]`. Then a new router works with old and new workers. Neither in-repo client has shipped: #32729 is open and #39610's example is open. So they can take the dual parse before this lands and only external clients written against the two frame layout would break.

### Phase 3: LoRA name and namespaced event hashes

These two go together. Adding `lora_name` without the hash change would give llm-d two keys for one engine hash.

**3a.** Carry the adapter name to the tree node, either as a `RadixKey` field or through a lookup in the scheduler's LoRA manager. Fill `lora_name`. With LoRA, put the name first in each `extra_keys` entry, as vLLM does.

**3b.** When `extra_key` is set, seed event hashes with the full namespace, the same way storage hashes do. Keep the current `sglang-cache-salt-v1` seed when only a salt is set, so salted hashes don't change. Mirror it in the Rust tree core.

**sgl-router cost:** its request side hash has no namespace. Today LoRA requests match base model blocks which can't be reused anyway. After 3b they match nothing until the router hashes with the namespace. That's a follow-up in `kv_events/hash.rs`.

### Not proposed

- **Renaming `CPU_PINNED` to `CPU`.** llm-d weights unknown tier names like GPU, so `cpu_pinned` scores 1.0 instead of 0.8. But sgl-router drops stores whose `medium` it doesn't know (`Tiers::for_store`, `kv_events/tree.rs`), so a  rename would turn off host-tier routing on older routers. llm-d users can set `kvCacheBackendConfigs: [{name: cpu_pinned, weight: 0.8}]` instead. See open question 1.
- **Unsigned hashes.** vLLM sends unsigned 64-bit and SGLang sends signed. llm-d accepts both (llm-d-router#2601 widens that). sgl-router decodes `i64`, so flipping would break it.
- **A vLLM hash recipe or `--kv-events-format vllm`.** llm-d doesn't recompute engine hashes and sgl-router depends on SGLang's recipe. Two formats would be a second thing to test with no consumer asking for it.
- **`group_idx` / `kv_cache_spec_kind`.** llm-d indexes events without `group_idx` as-is. Sending `group_idx` without a kind would make llm-d skip every store.

## Compatibility

| Change | vLLM-typed decoders | llm-d `vllm` adapter | sgl-router (main) | sgl-router replay (#32729) | #39610 docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1a `lora_name`, required `medium` | Fixed | No change until phase 3 | Ignored | n/a | Add field |
| 1b `extra_keys` salt | Reads it | Salted routing fixed | Ignored | n/a | Add field |
| 2 Replay topic frame | n/a | Replay works | n/a | Needs dual parse | Update example |
| 3a `lora_name` filled | Reads it | LoRA indexed under adapter name | Ignored | n/a | Update |
| 3b Namespaced hashes | n/a | `BlockRemoved` unambiguous | LoRA misses until router follow-up | n/a | Note |

## Out of scope

- **Multimodal.** SGLang replaces image tokens with hash derived pad values, so `token_ids` differ from vLLM's placeholders. `extra_keys` can't fix that.
- **EAGLE bigram `token_ids`.** Tracked separately.
- **Pages smaller than llm-d's block size** (llm-d-router#2235).
- **A removal reason on `BlockRemoved`** (#39604). It's additive but it would be worth proposing to vLLM too so the schemas don't drift again.

## Open questions

1. **Tier names.** Keep `CPU_PINNED` and document the llm-d weight? Or have sgl-router accept `CPU` first and switch the engine a release later?
2. **LoRA name source.** A `RadixKey` field which also needs the Rust core or a scheduler side lookup?
3. **LoRA in `extra_keys`.** llm-d's `ParseRawExtraKeys` reads bare strings as multimodal hashes which looks like it would fold a vLLM `lora_name` into keys the request side never adds. That isn't verified. Should SGLang match vLLM anyway or wait until llm-d settles it?
4. **Snapshots.** Should snapshot payloads from #33394 / #34407 use the same event schema?


# Related resources

- #27682: original request for `cache_salt` in `extra_keys`
- #37482: tagged-map events, `cache_salt` and `session_id` fields
- #39610: KV events docs page (open)
- #32729: sgl-router KV event gap replay (open)
- #33394, #34407: recoverable KV placement state with snapshots
- #39604: removal reason on `BlockRemoved`
- vllm-project/vllm#42892: vLLM events switched to maps
- vllm-project/vllm#45177: topic frame in vLLM replay replies
- vllm-project/vllm#51381: `session_id` on vLLM `BlockStored`
- llm-d/llm-d-router `pkg/kvevents/engineadapter/vllm_adapter.go`: map aware decoder SGLang events already pass through
- llm-d/llm-d-router#2235: pages smaller than the llm-d block size
- llm-d/llm-d-router#2601: hash integer conversion

### Checklist

- [x] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

First-time **Download & prepare ASR** hits `huggingface.co`, which is often blocked in mainland China. Finder launches do not inherit shell `HF_ENDPOINT`.

Please add an optional **Settings → Local speech model** field (e.g. `https://hf-mirror.com`), persist it, pass it to `snapshot_download` and the ASR child, and mention the mirror in the download-failure message. Cached weights should stay offline. A bad URL should fail Prepare, not dictation.

- Common mirror: https://hf-mirror.com

MEDIUM.title: [RFC] Core AI POC vs MLX-mini on Apple Silicon
MEDIUM.body:
## Motivation

show the **Apple Core AI** poc resutls.

[#1967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1967) already tracks first-class Apple Silicon support as **MLX (performance) + Torch/MPS (compatibility)**. Core AI is a third contract: compiled `*.aimodel` bundles, macOS 27+ system runtime, persistent KV inside Core AI, currently batch-one / greedy. It should not be folded into the model-support table in #1967 until we agree on POC scope.

This issue is the place to decide:
1. What a **bounded Core AI POC** looks like (and what it is not).
2. Why the deocode latency can not match our expection

## What we already measured

Public PoC: `adityavaid/sglang` @ `55c8cf4`, model `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`.

**M1 Pro 32 GB, macOS 27.0**, 1024-ctx batch=1 median decode step (warmup, then 128 decode tokens):

| Backend | Median decode | tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MLX `mlx_q4` (group 64) | 6.77 ms | ~148 |
| MLX default BF16/fp | 10.89 ms | ~92 |
| Core AI native INT4 | 23.59 ms | ~42 |
| Core AI native FP16 | 26.18 ms | ~38 |


## Proposed POC (bounded)

Treat Core AI as an **experiment + regression sentinel**, not a production Omni backend.

In scope:

- Qwen3-0.6B only, native forward, FP16 and optional INT4 .
- macOS 27 + Apple Silicon gate (`poc.py probe` / specialization).
- Batch=1 1024-ctx per-step decode vs MLX float and `mlx_q4` on the same host.


## Related
@adityavaid Thank you for this Core AI serving PoC, especially the `coreai-opt` authoring path.

- Apple Silicon roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1967
- Hardware reports (optional extra hosts): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/2158

Please comment with disagreements on scope, especially whether Omni should take a Core AI dependency.

HIGH.title: [Feature] Qwen3.5 multimodal (vision) path — M2
HIGH.body:
Part of the Qwen3.5 model series roadmap (#1421). Discharges #1007 §7–§9 (vision tower + multimodal pipeline). **Status: blocked** — see Depends on.

## Motivation

Qwen3.5's larger checkpoints carry a Qwen3-VL-Moe vision tower whose output is injected into the language model (a pooled image embedding at image-token positions, plus *deepstack* features added as residuals into the first decoder layers). The current Qwen3.5 LLM path is **text-only**: it embeds `input_ids`, holds `self.visual = None`, and hard-asserts `pixel_values is None` (`qwen3_5.py`). M2 adds the vision path so Qwen3.5 serves image+text end to end — this means *building* the injection path, not reusing an existing one.

Note: #1007's original framing used a staged, two-mesh disaggregated pipeline. The repo's multimodal direction has since converged on a **unified in-model VLM** path on the standard `srt/` pipeline (request handling in #1390, scheduling + forward in #1393). M2 follows that unified direction.

## Scope (four reviewable parts)

The architecture/config survey in part 1 is the best first contribution — it needs no TPU or serving access.

1. **Model / config registration.** A first-class survey of the exact Qwen3.5-VL ViT architecture and config nesting (`visual` / `vision_config` layout, deepstack indexes, merger family) is a **prerequisite deliverable** before implementation. Register the multimodal entry class and config.
2. **Processor / input plumbing.** Wire the Qwen-VL processor path (`pixel_values`, `image_grid_thw`, image-token offsets, 3D M-RoPE positions) into the unified request flow via the `MultimodalInputs` contract from #1390.
3. **Vision-feature injection (new code).** Build the Qwen3-VL-Moe ViT (3D patch embedding, learnable interpolated position embeddings, 2D-RoPE blocks, deepstack patch mergers) and **add the injection hooks the text path lacks today**: merge the pooler at image-token positions and add deepstack residuals into the early decoder layers; replace the `pixel_values is None` assert with the real forward.
4. **Eval smoke.** Image input exercised through the serving API, plus MMMU / MMBench accuracy.

**Out**
- Audio / video-generation / diffusion paths.
- Colocated-vs-disaggregated placement tuning (#1007 §11.4) — a later benchmark decision, not a correctness item.

## Depends on / aligns with (the blocker)

M2 is the Qwen3.5 adopter of multimodal work already in flight, and should reuse it rather than fork:

- #1390 — RFC: Multimodal Request Flow Design (Stage 1) — `MultimodalInputs` contract.
- #1398 — Stage 1 Qwen-VL multimodal preprocessing path.
- #1393 — RFC: in-model VLM scheduling & forward (closed; reference/alignment for the unified-path design, not an active blocker).
- #1302 — MiMo-V2.5 vision encoder: the closest ViT precedent (3D patch embed, 2D-RoPE, patch merger, windowed/GQA vision attention). Extract the shared encoder pieces so a non-omni model can import them without the audio stack.
- #1363 — MMMU-Pro evaluation support (the accuracy harness for the gate).

## Acceptance

- **Survey deliverable:** a written Qwen3.5-VL architecture + config-nesting spec accepted before implementation starts.
- **Vision-tower parity:** `pooler_output`, `deepstack_features`, `last_hidden_state` vs the HF reference within bf16 tolerance across single-image / multi-image / video grid fixtures.
- **Serving-API test:** an image+text request through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` API returns plausible output; request and recurrent slots freed on completion (not only in-process model construction).
- **Accuracy:** MMMU / MMBench within tolerance of the published Qwen3.5 numbers.

## References

- #1007 §7–§9 — vision tower + multimodal pipeline + time-sequence
- #1390 / #1398 — unified multimodal request flow + Qwen-VL preprocessing
- #1393 — in-model VLM scheduling & forward
- #1302 — MiMo-V2.5 vision encoder
- #1363 — MMMU-Pro evaluation

**Out**
- Audio / video-generation / diffusion paths.
- Colocated-vs-disaggregated placement tuning (#1007 §11.4) — a later benchmark decision, not a correctness item.

## Depends on / aligns with (the blocker)

M2 is the Qwen3.5 adopter of multimodal work already in flight, and should reuse it rather than fork:

- #1390 — RFC: Multimodal Request Flow Design (Stage 1) — `MultimodalInputs` contract.
- #1398 — Stage 1 Qwen-VL multimodal preprocessing path.
- #1393 — RFC: in-model VLM scheduling & forward (closed; reference/alignment for the unified-path design, not an active blocker).
- #1302 — MiMo-V2.5 vision encoder: the closest ViT precedent (3D patch embed, 2D-RoPE, patch merger, windowed/GQA vision attention). Extract the shared encoder pieces so a non-omni model can import them without the audio stack.
- #1363 — MMMU-Pro evaluation support (the accuracy harness for the gate).

- **Survey deliverable:** a written Qwen3.5-VL architecture + config-nesting spec accepted before implementation starts.
- **Vision-tower parity:** `pooler_output`, `deepstack_features`, `last_hidden_state` vs the HF reference within bf16 tolerance across single-image / multi-image / video grid fixtures.
- **Serving-API test:** an image+text request through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` API returns plausible output; request and recurrent slots freed on completion (not only in-process model construction).
- **Accuracy:** MMMU / MMBench within tolerance of the published Qwen3.5 numbers.

- #1007 §7–§9 — vision tower + multimodal pipeline + time-sequence
- #1390 / #1398 — unified multimodal request flow + Qwen-VL preprocessing
- #1393 — in-model VLM scheduling & forward
- #1302 — MiMo-V2.5 vision encoder

HIGH.title: [Feature]: Add OCI Generative AI as a first-class LLM provider
HIGH.body:
### Problem or Motivation

OCI Generative AI exposes an OpenAI-compatible Responses API, but configuring it in OpenHands currently requires advanced/manual settings and knowledge of OCI-specific endpoint, project, and capability requirements. Although OpenHands inherits provider discovery from LiteLLM, there is no first-class OCI profile or guided setup, making OCI-hosted and enterprise deployments difficult to configure reliably.

### Desired Behavior

Add OCI Generative AI as a first-class provider in Agent Canvas and the underlying SDK profile system.

For the initial scope, users should provide:

- OCI region
- Generative AI project OCID
- Model ID
- OCI Generative AI API key

OpenHands should derive the regional `/openai/v1` base URL, send the project identifier correctly, and use the Responses API without requiring manual headers or capability overrides. Model IDs should remain manually enterable because availability varies by region.

OCI IAM authentication through session, user, instance, or resource principals can be handled in a follow-up.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] OCI Generative AI is selectable when creating or editing an LLM profile.
- [ ] The profile supports region, project OCID, model ID, and GenAI API key.
- [ ] The API key is encrypted/redacted consistently with other provider secrets.
- [ ] OpenHands derives the correct regional OCI endpoint and supplies the project identifier.
- [ ] A supported OCI model completes a normal Responses API request.
- [ ] An end-to-end conversation successfully invokes at least one OpenHands function tool and consumes its result.
- [ ] Users can manually enter model IDs, with links to OCI's model and region documentation.
- [ ] Setup documentation includes the required OCI project and IAM policy prerequisites.
- [ ] Configuration serialization and request construction have automated tests; a credential-gated live integration test is documented or added.

### Alternatives Considered

- Configure OCI manually as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This is possible in principle, but requires users to know the endpoint, project header, and Responses API capability settings.
- Use LiteLLM's native `oci/...` provider. It already exists, but OpenHands does not expose its OCI-specific parameters, and there is an open LiteLLM issue involving coding-agent tool schemas.

### Additional Context

- [OCI Generative AI quick start](https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm)
- [OCI models and regional availability](https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agentic-regions.htm)
- [OCI tool support](https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/tool-support.htm)
- [LiteLLM OCI tool-calling issue](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/31449)

LOW.title: Dockerfile best practice: specify non-root USER in custom tool example Dockerfile
LOW.body:
## Context

The Dockerfile at `examples/02_remote_agent_server/06_custom_tool/Dockerfile` does not currently specify a `USER` directive, so the container runs as `root` by default.

## Best practice

It is a Docker best practice to run containers as a non-root user. Adding a `USER` directive with a non-root user avoids unnecessary privilege and follows community conventions for well-formed Dockerfiles.

## Suggested change

Add a non-root user to the Dockerfile, e.g.:

```dockerfile
RUN useradd -m appuser
USER appuser
```

Or use an existing non-root user if one is already created in the base image.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dockerfile includes a `USER` directive with a non-root user
- [ ] Container still builds and runs correctly
